previous_reviews.reason: "Graph layout" is misleading in a visual editor. The worker compiles the model for inference and initializes the engine state, including any sampled-message preparation. It loads the saved bundle and reads the data-port contract inside this timing. Drawing the on-screen diagram is not part of the measurement; binding observations and timing inference follow afterward.

profile.compile.jaxpr_trace_duration.draft: Total time JAX spent tracing functions into jaxpr, its representation of array operations, while setting up and running this model. The worker adds up all reported trace durations before the separate executable analysis.
profile.compile.jaxpr_trace_duration.text: This element is the total time JAX spent tracing Python functions into jaxpr, its internal representation of array math, while setting up and running this model. The worker adds together all reported trace times recorded before the separate executable analysis runs.

profile.compile.jaxpr_to_mlir_module_dur.draft: Total time JAX spent lowering jaxpr into MLIR compiler modules while setting up and running this model. This sums the durations reported for individual compilations before the separate executable analysis.
profile.compile.jaxpr_to_mlir_module_dur.text: This element is the total time JAX spent translating jaxpr array programs into MLIR compiler modules while setting up and running this model. It sums the times reported across individual compilations before the separate executable analysis.

profile.compile.backend_compile_duration.draft: Total time JAX attributed to backend compilation while setting up and running this model. The backend turns lowered programs into device executables. The worker records this total before the separate analysis of individual schedule units.
profile.compile.backend_compile_duration.text: This element is the total time JAX spent in backend compilation, turning translated compiler modules into runnable device executables while setting up and running this model. The worker totals these durations before running the separate analysis of individual schedule steps.

profile.compile.other.draft: Total duration of this named JAX compilation stage while the worker set up and ran this revision. The value adds time across reported events, and can overlap the setup and inference timers.
profile.compile.other.text: This element is the total time spent in this specific named JAX compilation stage while the worker set up and ran this revision. It adds up durations across reported events and can overlap with the setup and inference timers.

profile.executable.flooding_step.draft: XLA’s estimated floating-point operations and bytes accessed for one synchronous sweep of this model. All factors read the previous messages. Studio analyzes this unit even when the selected inference schedule uses a different update order.
profile.executable.flooding_step.text: This element is the XLA compiler's estimate of floating-point calculations and memory bytes accessed during one simultaneous (flooding) update sweep of this model, where all factors read the previous step's messages. Studio analyzes this step even if the model's chosen inference schedule uses a different update order.

profile.executable.two_pass_exact.draft: XLA’s estimated floating-point operations and bytes accessed for this model’s exact tree calculation. It passes messages inward and outward, checks the result with a synchronous sweep, and includes support and applicable free-energy checks.
profile.executable.two_pass_exact.text: This element is the XLA compiler's estimate of floating-point calculations and memory bytes accessed for this model's exact tree pass. That calculation sends messages inward and outward, verifies the result with one simultaneous sweep, and includes support checks plus any applicable free-energy checks.

profile.executable.colored_step.draft: XLA’s estimated floating-point operations and bytes accessed for one sweep over the model’s cyclic belief-propagation components. Independent factors update together within a color, and later colors see earlier updates.
profile.executable.colored_step.text: This element is XLA's estimated floating-point operations and bytes accessed for one pass (sweep) over the model's looped belief-propagation parts. Independent factors update together within each color group, and later groups use the earlier updates.

profile.executable.mixed_step.draft: XLA’s estimated floating-point operations and bytes accessed for one mixed sweep. It updates the iterative factors, then refreshes belief-propagation components with tree passes or a colored sweep.
profile.executable.mixed_step.text: This element is XLA's estimated floating-point operations and bytes accessed for one mixed sweep. That sweep updates the iterative factors, then refreshes the belief-propagation parts using tree passes or a colored sweep.

profile.executable.colored_prime.draft: XLA’s estimated floating-point operations and bytes accessed for priming the tree components before this model’s colored iteration begins. Priming passes messages in both directions through those trees.
profile.executable.colored_prime.text: This element is XLA's estimated floating-point operations and bytes accessed for initializing (priming) the tree-structured parts before this model's colored iteration begins. Priming sends messages in both directions through those trees.

profile.executable.mixed_prime.draft: XLA’s estimated floating-point operations and bytes accessed for priming the belief-propagation components before mixed iteration. Tree components receive two passes and cyclic components a colored sweep.
profile.executable.mixed_prime.text: This element is XLA's estimated floating-point operations and bytes accessed for initializing (priming) the belief-propagation parts before mixed iteration. Tree-structured parts get two passes, and looped parts get a colored sweep.

profile.executable.other.draft: XLA’s estimate of the floating-point operations and bytes accessed by one invocation of this named unit for the measured model. A diagnostic appears when the backend cannot supply the estimate.
profile.executable.other.text: This element is XLA's estimate of the floating-point operations and bytes accessed by one call to this named unit for the measured model. A diagnostic message appears when the backend cannot provide the estimate.

profile.lowerCompile.draft: The first time measures lowering this model’s named schedule unit into compiler IR. The second measures the call that produces its device executable. Studio times these calls during the separate executable analysis after benchmarking.
profile.lowerCompile.text: This element is two timings: the first measures translating (lowering) this model's named schedule unit into compiler intermediate representation (IR), and the second measures the call that builds its device executable. Studio records these times during the separate executable analysis after benchmarking.

profile.buffers.draft: XLA’s planned temporary workspace and peak device buffer bytes for this executable. The peak adds input, output and temporary bytes and subtracts storage shared by inputs and outputs. Both numbers describe the compiler’s plan for one unit.
profile.buffers.text: This element is XLA's planned temporary workspace and peak device buffer memory for this executable, formatted in MiB or GiB. The peak combines input, output, and temporary buffer memory minus storage shared between inputs and outputs, and both estimates describe the compiler's plan for one unit.

previous_reviews.text: This element is XLA's planned temporary workspace and peak device buffer memory in bytes for this executable. The peak totals input, output, and temporary bytes minus storage shared between inputs and outputs, and both numbers describe the compiler's plan for a single unit.
previous_reviews.reason: The UI formats these estimates in MiB or GiB. Explain the planned temporary and peak device memory for this executable without implying a raw byte count appears on screen.

trace.title.draft: The saved timeline belongs to a single job on a pinned model revision. It shows the latest worker events and, for inference, the solver’s final outcome.
trace.title.text: This element is the saved timeline for a single job tied to a fixed model revision. It shows the latest background worker events and, for inference jobs, the solver's final outcome.

trace.empty.draft: Start inference or open a saved job in Run history to see its timeline.
trace.empty.text: This element is a placeholder shown until a timeline is loaded. Start inference or open a saved job in Run history to see its timeline.

trace.chart.draft: Free energy is the model’s scored objective for the recorded beliefs, including the contributions of its factors and shared variables. The chart shows finite values. Missing or undefined values leave gaps.
trace.chart.text: This element is a chart of free energy, the model's scored objective for the recorded beliefs, including contributions from its factors and shared variables. It plots finite values, while missing or undefined values leave gaps.

trace.latest.draft: The most recent finite free-energy value in this run. An earlier sample stays visible here if a later sweep has no finite value.
trace.latest.text: This element is the most recent finite free-energy value in this run. An earlier sample remains displayed here if a later sweep has no finite value.

trace.axisSweep.draft: The horizontal axis follows sweep numbers. In an interactive trace each number is the iteration budget for a fresh replay from the same starting state. The line connects consecutive sweeps with finite energy.
trace.axisSweep.text: This element is the horizontal axis tracking sweep numbers. In an interactive trace, each number is the iteration budget for a fresh replay from the same starting state, and the line connects consecutive sweeps that have finite energy.

trace.axisSample.draft: The run recorded energy on fewer sweeps than it executed. These numbers count the energy samples in order, because the saved result does not identify their individual sweep numbers.
trace.axisSample.text: This element is an index counting the recorded energy samples in order. The run recorded energy on fewer sweeps than it ran, and the saved result does not record which sweep produced each sample.

trace.noEnergy.draft: A point appears only when the engine can assign a finite free energy to the beliefs. Early sweeps can lack a defined energy, and some jobs, such as generating observations, do not run inference.
trace.noEnergy.text: This element is a notice for runs without plottable energy points, since a point appears only when the engine can assign a finite free energy to the beliefs. Early sweeps may lack a defined energy, and some jobs, such as generating observations, do not run inference.

trace.recent.draft: The eight most recent recorded events appear newest first. They can include setup phases, trace replays, benchmark measurements, the final outcome or a worker error.
trace.recent.text: This element is a list of the eight most recent recorded events, ordered newest first. Entries can include setup phases, trace replays, benchmark measurements, the final outcome, or a worker error.

trace.phase.draft: The worker reports what it is doing. These milestones mark steps such as loading the pinned model, binding observations and starting a measurement.
trace.phase.text: This element is a milestone reporting what the worker is currently doing. It marks steps such as loading the pinned model, attaching observations, and starting a measurement.

trace.sweep.draft: The worker reruns inference from the same bound state with this iteration budget, then reports the final state of that replay. A replay can stop early if the solver converges.
trace.sweep.text: This element is a recorded inference replay for an increasing iteration budget, starting each time from the same observation-bound state. Each row reports end-of-replay measurements, and a replay can stop early if the solver converges.

previous_reviews.text: This element is an inference rerun starting from the same observation-bound state using this iteration budget. It reports that replay's final state, and the replay can stop early if the solver converges.
previous_reviews.reason: A sweep row reports measurements at the end of this replay, not the entire final state. Clarify that it is the recorded replay for an increasing iteration budget, starting each time from the same observation-bound state.

trace.fe.draft: The model’s free energy evaluated on the final state of this replay. A dash means the engine could not return a finite value for those beliefs.
trace.fe.text: This element is the model's free energy evaluated at the final state of this replay. A dash means the engine could not return a finite number for those beliefs.

trace.delta.draft: The last recorded change in the solver’s messages for this replay. A small change indicates that the messages are settling. The solver status records whether its convergence checks passed.
trace.delta.text: This element is the last recorded change in the solver's messages during this replay. A small change indicates that the messages are settling, while the solver status records whether convergence checks passed.

trace.replayTime.draft: Synchronized wall time for the entire replay from the initial state through this iteration budget. It can include compilation and time spent repeating earlier sweeps.
trace.replayTime.text: This element is the synchronized wall-clock time for the entire replay from the initial state through this iteration budget. It can include compilation and time spent repeating earlier sweeps.

trace.measurement.draft: A timed inference call in the benchmark worker. The first call supplies the cold timing. Repeated calls on the same starting state and data supply warm samples.
trace.measurement.text: This element is a timed inference call in the benchmark worker. The first call provides the cold timing, and repeated calls on the same starting state and data provide warm timing samples.

trace.warmTime.draft: Elapsed time for this individual warm inference call, including the wait for its resulting state to be ready.
trace.warmTime.text: This element is the elapsed time for this individual warm inference call. It includes the wait for the resulting state to become ready.

trace.finish.draft: The worker finished writing the job result. For inference, the solver status records whether it converged, exhausted its budget, diverged or found the model infeasible.
trace.finish.text: This element is the marker showing the worker finished writing the job result. For inference jobs, the solver status records whether the solver converged, exhausted its budget, diverged, or found the model infeasible.

trace.iterations.draft: The number of iterations the solver reports for the final inference result. It can be smaller than the requested budget if the solver stops early.
trace.iterations.text: This element is the number of iterations the solver reports for the final inference result. It can be smaller than the requested budget if the solver stops early.

trace.residual.draft: The solver’s final numerical measure of what remains to settle. The measure depends on the solver, for example the change in free energy or a fixed-point error. Read it with the final status.
trace.residual.text: This element is the solver's final numerical measure of how much remains to settle. Its definition depends on the solver, such as free-energy change or fixed-point error, so read it alongside the final status.

trace.error.draft: The worker or service reports the reason it could not complete the requested operation. The timeline retains any earlier events for this job.
trace.error.text: This element is the reported reason why the worker or service could not complete the requested operation. Any earlier events for this job remain in the timeline.

trace.status.job.draft: The latest execution state recorded for this worker. A trace can pause between replays. When inference finishes, this badge shows the engine’s termination outcome.
trace.status.job.text: This element is a badge showing the latest execution state recorded for this worker. A trace can pause between replays, and once inference finishes, this badge shows the engine's termination outcome.

trace.status.converged.draft: The inference engine met the convergence checks for this model’s solver. Exact schedules can certify a solution after a single execution.
trace.status.converged.text: This element is the status showing the inference engine met the convergence checks for this model's solver. Exact schedules can certify a solution after a single run.

trace.status.budget_exhausted.draft: The solver reached a work limit before it could certify convergence. The final beliefs and residual describe the state it reached.
trace.status.budget_exhausted.text: This element is the status showing the solver reached a work limit before it could certify convergence. The final beliefs and residual describe the state it reached.

trace.status.diverged.draft: The solver reported numerical divergence, such as a non-finite update or objective. Inspect the final result for any recorded failure reason or factor.
trace.status.diverged.text: This element is the status showing the solver reported numerical divergence, such as a non-finite update or objective value. Inspect the final result for any recorded failure reason or factor.

trace.status.infeasible.draft: The solver found incompatible evidence or constraints that left no feasible support. Inspect the failure details and the model’s observations.
trace.status.infeasible.text: This element is an indicator showing that the solver found conflicting evidence or constraints that left no valid solution (feasible support). Inspect the failure details and the model's observations to see what clashed.

trace.pause.draft: Request a pause before the next replay. A replay already running can finish before the worker waits.
trace.pause.text: This element is a button to request a pause before the next replay starts. Any replay that is already running can finish before the background worker waits.

trace.resume.draft: Allow the worker to replay successively larger iteration budgets from the same initial state until inference converges or the requested limit is reached.
trace.resume.text: This element is a button that lets the background worker run replays with successively larger step limits (iteration budgets) from the same starting state. It continues until the calculation settles (inference converges) or reaches the requested limit.

trace.step.draft: Permit one more replay with the next iteration budget, then leave playback paused unless the run has ended.
trace.step.text: This element is a button that runs one more replay using the next step limit (iteration budget). Playback then stays paused unless the run has already ended.

trace.cancel.draft: End this job and terminate its worker if it is running. Events already written remain available in Run history.
trace.cancel.text: This element is a button to end this job and stop its background worker if it is currently running. Any events already recorded remain available in Run history.

activity.revision.draft: This is the saved model revision you are viewing. Studio identifies it by the first eight characters of its revision hash.
activity.revision.text: This element is the saved model version (revision) you are currently viewing. Studio identifies it using the first eight characters of its unique revision hash.

activity.history.draft: Open this revision’s changes relative to the current model. The dialog lets you restore the earlier contents in a new revision.
activity.history.text: This element is a control to open the differences between this saved version (revision) and the current model. The dialog lets you restore the earlier contents as a new revision.

activity.review.draft: This review thread records its author, whether it is a critique or a proposed edit, and whether it is open or closed. The text and replies belong to this saved model.
activity.review.text: This element is a review thread showing its author, whether it is a critique or a proposed edit, and whether it is open or closed. Its text and replies belong to this saved model.

activity.reply.draft: Add a signed reply to this review thread and preview it before saving the revision.
activity.reply.text: This element is an action to add a reply to this review thread, credited to your account or agent identity. You can preview the reply before saving the revision.

previous_reviews.text: This element is an action to add a signed reply to this review thread. You can preview your reply before saving the new model revision.
previous_reviews.reason: Studio records who posted the reply using their account or agent identity. The reply itself is not cryptographically signed. Say who is credited without claiming a signature.

activity.accept.draft: Preview the proposed graph edits against the current model. Committing the preview applies the commands and marks the proposal accepted.
activity.accept.text: This element is an action to preview the proposed graph edits against the current model. Saving (committing) the preview applies those edit commands and marks the proposal accepted.

activity.decline.draft: Preview closing the proposal as declined. Committing records the decision and leaves its proposed graph edits unapplied.
activity.decline.text: This element is an action to preview closing this proposal as declined. Saving (committing) records that decision and leaves the proposed graph edits unapplied.

activity.resolve.draft: Preview marking this critique resolved. Committing records that outcome in the model’s review history.
activity.resolve.text: This element is an action to preview marking this critique as resolved. Saving (committing) records that outcome in the model's review history.

activity.job.draft: Open the timeline for this saved experiment. The row gives its kind, worker status, model revision and local creation time.
activity.job.text: This element is a row that opens the timeline for this saved experiment. It displays the experiment's kind, background worker status, model revision, and local creation time.

activity.generate.draft: Describe stochastic observations to generate Python simulator source for this model’s data ports. You can inspect the generated source before running it.
activity.generate.text: This element is a tool where you describe random (stochastic) observations to generate Python simulator code for this model's data inputs (ports). You can inspect the generated source code before running it.

activity.simulate.draft: Open the source editor to run a NumPy simulator with a seed and parameters. Studio validates its observation tape against the pinned model’s data ports.
activity.simulate.text: This element is a control that opens the code editor to run a NumPy simulator using a random seed and parameters. Studio checks the resulting sequence of observations (observation tape) against the pinned model's data inputs (ports).

activity.inspectSource.draft: Open this job’s generated Python source in the simulator editor. Review or edit the code, seed and parameters before running it to produce observations.
activity.inspectSource.text: This element is an action that opens this job's generated Python source code in the simulator editor. You can review or edit the code, random seed, and parameters before running it to generate observations.

activity.tape.draft: Open inference with this simulator job as its observation tape. The worker loads the recorded values and checks that they fit the selected model’s data ports.
activity.tape.text: This element is an action that opens inference using this simulator job as the observation tape (recorded data). The background worker loads these recorded values and checks that they match the selected model's data inputs (ports).

activity.beliefs.draft: Open the saved posterior summaries by variable for this result. Depending on the family, these include categorical weights, Gaussian means and marginal variances, or exponential-family and Dirichlet parameters.
activity.beliefs.text: This element is an action that opens the saved variable-by-variable posterior belief summaries for this result. Depending on the distribution family, these include categorical weights, Gaussian means and individual (marginal) variances, or exponential-family and Dirichlet parameters.

activity.measurement.draft: Inspect the full result JSON saved by this job. Inference results include the observation digest, seed, schedule, device, solver outcome and numerical traces.
activity.measurement.text: This element is an action that lets you inspect the full result JSON saved by this job. For inference results, this includes the observation digest (summary hash), random seed, schedule, compute device, solver outcome, and numerical traces.
